claims.text: Reducing laser power from 200 W to 150 W and increasing scanning speed from 500 mm/s to 700 mm/s will improve the dimensional precision of laser-powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components.
The specified parameter changes will improve the mechanical integrity of laser-powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components.
The specified parameter changes will reduce fabrication-induced defects in laser-powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components.
As-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components may contain fabrication defects.
The proposed effect applies at 150 W laser power, 700 mm/s scanning speed, 30 μm layer thickness, and 0° build orientation.
The optimized parameters will reduce residual stresses.
The optimized parameters will reduce porosity.
Reducing laser power and increasing scanning speed will reduce energy input.
Reducing laser power and increasing scanning speed will increase the cooling rate.
The reduced energy input and increased cooling rate will produce a more uniform microstructure.
Dimensional precision will improve by 15% relative to fabrication at 200 W and 500 mm/s.
Mechanical integrity will improve by 20% relative to fabrication at 200 W and 500 mm/s.
Fabrication-induced defects will decrease by 30% relative to fabrication at 200 W and 500 mm/s.
Laser power of 200 W and scanning speed of 500 mm/s constitute the current fabrication baseline.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the specific high-entropy-alloy composition and application conditions.
